360	def _validate_route_walk(
361	    grid: GridMap,
362	    origin: Position,
363	    route: Sequence[object],
364	    *,
365	    robot_id: str,
366	    checkpoint: bool,
367	    blocked_cells: frozenset[Position] | None = None,
368	) -> list[Position]:
369	    """Validate one robot's remaining route as a cell-by-cell map walk.
370	
371	    This is the single place that owns the walking rule shared by direct
372	    fleet construction and checkpoint recovery, so the same legality check is
373	    never edited twice. A route holds the cells still ahead of *origin*:
374	
375	    * every waypoint must parse as two plain integers (booleans are rejected),
376	      and lie inside the map -- a cell in *blocked_cells* is the one kind of
377	      currently obstructed waypoint a version 2 checkpoint recovery may carry
378	      (see below), everything else off the traversable map is rejected;
379	    * the first waypoint must be an up/down/left/right neighbour of *origin*,
380	      so a first waypoint equal to the current cell is rejected;
381	    * every later waypoint must be exactly one orthogonal step from the
382	      previous one -- diagonal moves, multi-cell jumps and two identical
383	      consecutive waypoints are all rejected.
384	
385	    Detours and revisits (including *origin*) are legal, and a route crossing
386	    another robot's cell is never a walk error: traffic is settled while
387	    stepping, not here. The walkability rule deliberately says nothing about
388	    the bound task's pickup/dropoff requirements; checkpoint loading keeps
389	    that separate, stricter business check. The result is a fresh mutable list
390	    of tuple cells, so validating never aliases or mutates the caller's
391	    container and a rejected input leaves every earlier object untouched.
392	
393	    *blocked_cells* is honoured only for checkpoint recovery and names the
394	    cells the recorded map-change history explains: cells open on the base map
395	    that an accepted edit has since closed and that are still closed at save
396	    time. A taskless robot's preset route may legitimately end on such a cell
397	    -- the robot keeps its unconsumed waypoints and simply waits before it --
398	    so those waypoints walk as well as the open cells do. The exemption is
399	    deliberately narrow: only checkpoint loading ever supplies the set (direct
400	    construction leaves it ``None``), only a robot without a bound task may
401	    use it (the caller never passes the set for a task route), and the cells
402	    must be inside the map -- an out-of-bounds waypoint is rejected regardless.
403	    A blocked cell in the base map that no edit explains is never part of the
404	    set, so a route crossing an initial or unexplained obstacle stays illegal.
405	
406	    The two entries keep their existing format and wording differences via
407	    *checkpoint*: direct construction (false) accepts a list or tuple route of
408	    list-or-tuple cells and reports ``route waypoint N`` with a dedicated
409	    message for a first waypoint on the current cell and for repeated
410	    consecutive waypoints; checkpoint loading (true) keeps the strict JSON
411	    list-of-lists format (``_as_pair``), says ``route entry`` and folds both
412	    equal-cell cases into its existing non-adjacency message. The checks
413	    performed are identical either way.
414	    """
415	    allowed_blocked = frozenset() if blocked_cells is None else blocked_cells
416	    waypoints: list[Position] = []
417	    previous = origin
418	    for index, cell in enumerate(route):
419	        if checkpoint:
420	            waypoint = _as_pair(
421	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {index}"
422	            )
423	        else:
424	            waypoint = _as_cell(
425	                cell, f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index}"
426	            )
427	        if not grid.contains(waypoint) or (
428	            waypoint in grid.obstacles and waypoint not in allowed_blocked
429	        ):
430	            if checkpoint:
431	                raise ValueError(
432	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route entry {list(waypoint)} is "
433	                    "outside the map or inside an obstacle"
434	                )
435	            raise ValueError(
436	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint {index} "
437	                f"{list(waypoint)} is outside the map or inside an obstacle"
438	            )
439	        if waypoint == previous:
440	            if checkpoint:
441	                # The checkpoint wording treats an equal cell like any other
442	                # non-adjacent step, naming both cells of the offending move.
443	                raise ValueError(
444	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
445	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
446	                )
447	            if index == 0:
448	                raise ValueError(
449	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)} "
450	                    "is the robot's current cell; the remaining route must "
451	                    "start with the next cell"
452	                )
453	            raise ValueError(
454	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route repeats cell {list(waypoint)} at "
455	                f"consecutive waypoints {index - 1} and {index}"
456	            )
457	        if (
458	            abs(waypoint[0] - previous[0])
459	            + abs(waypoint[1] - previous[1])
460	            != 1
461	        ):
462	            if checkpoint:
463	                raise ValueError(
464	                    f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently from "
465	                    f"{list(previous)} to {list(waypoint)}"
466	                )
467	            if index == 0:
468	                segment = (
469	                    f"from its current position {list(previous)} to route "
470	                    f"waypoint 0 {list(waypoint)}"
471	                )
472	            else:
473	                segment = (
474	                    f"from route waypoint {index - 1} {list(previous)} to "
475	                    f"waypoint {index} {list(waypoint)}"
476	                )
477	            raise ValueError(
478	                f"robot {robot_id!r} route moves non-adjacently {segment}: "
479	                "every step must move one orthogonal cell"
480	            )
481	        waypoints.append(waypoint)
482	        previous = waypoint
483	    return waypoints

520	            # routes must not be re-checked here against the saved grid, where
521	            # those legitimate waypoints look obstructed. Every other
522	            # constructor check above still runs.

525	        # spelled them: a mutable list of tuple cells. The normalized copies are

527	        # (even one buried in a later robot's route) never touches the caller's

533	    @staticmethod
534	    def _validate_task_ownership(robots: Sequence[Robot], tasks: Sequence[Task]) -> None:
535	        """Reject impossible initial bindings between robots and tasks.
536	
537	        The very same mutual-ownership requirement backs direct construction
538	        and checkpoint loading, so it lives in exactly one place. The binding
539	        only governs work still in progress:
540	
541	        * A robot that declares a task must name a task that exists, is not
542	          completed yet, and is assigned back to that same robot.
543	        * An unfinished task that names an owner must name an existing robot
544	          whose current task it is; an unfinished task with the goods already
545	          collected additionally must have an owner.
546	        * A robot can therefore never be claimed by two unfinished tasks: the
547	          second task's owner points at a robot that executes another task.
548	
549	        Completed tasks only keep *historical* ownership: their recorded
550	        ``assigned_robot`` is not required to be idle or to name them back, so
551	        a robot that already finished one task may be idle or busy with a new
552	        one. Unassigned, not-yet-collected tasks simply wait -- even when no
553	        robot can reach them -- and are not an ownership error. Nothing here
554	        rewrites a binding or drops a task; an inconsistent input is rejected
555	        as a whole with a :class:`ValueError` naming the conflicting robot or
556	        task, leaving the caller's objects untouched.
557	        """
558	        robot_by_id = {robot.robot_id: robot for robot in robots}
559	        task_by_id = {task.task_id: task for task in tasks}
560	        for robot in robots:
561	            if robot.task_id is None:
562	                continue
563	            task = task_by_id.get(robot.task_id)
564	            if task is None:
565	                raise ValueError(
566	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes unknown task "
567	                    f"{robot.task_id!r}"
568	                )
569	            if task.completed:
570	                raise ValueError(
571	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
572	                    "that is already completed"
573	                )
574	            if task.assigned_robot != robot.robot_id:
575	                raise ValueError(
576	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} executes task {task.task_id!r} "
577	                    f"but the task is assigned to {task.assigned_robot!r}"
578	                )
579	        for task in tasks:
580	            # Completed tasks retain historical ownership; their robots are
581	            # free to take new work, so the mutual binding only holds while a
582	            # task is still in progress.
583	            if task.completed:
584	                continue
585	            if task.picked_up and task.assigned_robot is None:
586	                raise ValueError(
587	                    f"task {task.task_id!r} is picked up but has no assigned robot"
588	                )
589	            if task.assigned_robot is not None:
590	                owner = robot_by_id.get(task.assigned_robot)
591	                if owner is None:
592	                    raise ValueError(
593	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} is assigned to unknown robot "
594	                        f"{task.assigned_robot!r}"
595	                    )
596	                if owner.task_id != task.task_id:
597	                    raise ValueError(
598	                        f"task {task.task_id!r} claims robot {owner.robot_id!r} "
599	                        f"but the robot executes {owner.task_id!r}"
600	                    )

602	    @staticmethod
603	    def _normalize_initial_routes(
604	        grid: GridMap, robots: Sequence[Robot]
605	    ) -> list[list[Position]]:
606	        """Validate every remaining route and return normalized copies.
607	
608	        Every robot is checked, idle or task-bound, via the single shared walk
609	        validator :func:`_validate_route_walk` -- the same coordinate shape,
610	        map-walkability and one-orthogonal-step rule checkpoint recovery uses
611	        -- so a walking rule never has to be changed in two places. The outer
612	        route may be a list or tuple and each waypoint may itself be a list or
613	        tuple of two plain integers -- booleans are not integers here, and
614	        wrong lengths or element types raise :class:`ValueError` instead of
615	        leaking unpacking or hashing failures. The forms may be mixed freely;
616	        only the coordinate order matters, not the container types.
617	
618	        Accepted routes are returned as mutable lists of tuple cells, the one
619	        shape the rest of the engine relies on (head consumption with
620	        ``pop(0)`` and hashable cells for road and occupancy checks). Empty
621	        lists and tuples both normalize to an empty route. Routes need not be
622	        shortest paths and may revisit cells, and traffic (a route crossing
623	        another robot's cell, or routes sharing a cell) is left to execution:
624	        only walkability on the given map is judged.
625	
626	        The check is read-only -- :func:`_validate_route_walk` builds fresh
627	        lists, and the caller commits them itself only once every robot has
628	        passed, so a rejected fleet is rejected as a whole: an error on a
629	        later robot or at the end of a route never truncates, pads, reorders
630	        or otherwise modifies an earlier robot or any caller object. The
631	        shared walk check says nothing about tasks; direct construction keeps
632	        accepting any walkable route, while checkpoint loading keeps its own
633	        stricter validation that also covers the pickup/dropoff rules.
634	        """
635	        normalized: list[list[Position]] = []
636	        for robot in robots:
637	            route = robot.route
638	            if not isinstance(route, (list, tuple)):
639	                raise ValueError(
640	                    f"robot {robot.robot_id!r} remaining route must be a list "
641	                    "of [x, y] waypoints"
642	                )
643	            normalized.append(
644	                _validate_route_walk(
645	                    grid,
646	                    robot.position,
647	                    route,
648	                    robot_id=robot.robot_id,
649	                    checkpoint=False,
650	                )
651	            )
652	        return normalized

655	    # Dynamic map edits

658	    def modify_obstacles(
659	        self,
660	        added: Sequence[Position] = (),
661	        removed: Sequence[Position] = (),
662	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
663	        """Close and/or reopen cells without advancing the simulation.
664	
665	        The whole request is validated before anything changes: coordinates
666	        must be two plain integers (booleans are rejected), lie inside the
667	        map, no cell may appear in both lists, and newly added obstacles may
668	        not cover a robot's current cell. Duplicate coordinates inside one
669	        batch are processed once. Adding an existing obstacle or removing a
670	        traversable cell is a no-op. Invalid requests raise :class:`ValueError`
671	        and leave every part of the state untouched.
672	
673	        Assigned unfinished tasks keep their robot: routes are replanned
674	        against the new map, or, when a required point is unreachable, cleared
675	        while the task is suspended. No tick is recorded, no robot moves and no
676	        distance is accumulated.
677	        """
678	        add_cells = self._normalize_cells(added, "added")
679	        remove_cells = self._normalize_cells(removed, "removed")
680	        conflict = set(add_cells) & set(remove_cells)
681	        if conflict:
682	            cell = sorted(conflict)[0]
683	            raise ValueError(
684	                f"cell {list(cell)} is both added and removed in the same request"
685	            )
686	        occupied = {robot.position for robot in self.robots.values()}
687	        for cell in add_cells:
688	            if cell in occupied:
689	                raise ValueError(
690	                    f"cannot add obstacle at {list(cell)}: a robot currently occupies it"
691	                )
692	        return self._apply_map_change(add_cells, remove_cells)
693	
694	    def _normalize_cells(self, cells: Sequence[Position], label: str) -> list[Position]:
695	        if isinstance(cells, (str, bytes)) or not isinstance(cells, (list, tuple)):
696	            raise ValueError(f"{label} cells must be provided as a list of [x, y] pairs")
697	        seen: set[Position] = set()
698	        ordered: list[Position] = []
699	        for index, cell in enumerate(cells):
700	            position = _as_cell(cell, f"{label} cell {index}")
701	            if not self.grid.contains(position):
702	                raise ValueError(f"{label} cell {list(position)} lies outside the map")
703	            if position in seen:
704	                # Batch-internal duplicates are handled once, not rejected.
705	                continue
706	            seen.add(position)
707	            ordered.append(position)
708	        return ordered
709	
710	    def _apply_map_change(
711	        self, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
712	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
713	        obstacles = set(self.grid.obstacles)
714	        actual_added = [cell for cell in added if cell not in obstacles]
715	        obstacles.update(actual_added)
716	        actual_removed = [cell for cell in removed if cell in obstacles]
717	        obstacles.difference_update(actual_removed)
718	        if not actual_added and not actual_removed:
719	            return self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, [], [])
720	
721	        # Everything below only runs once the batch was fully validated and is
722	        # known to change the map.
723	        self.grid = GridMap(self.grid.width, self.grid.height, frozenset(obstacles))
724	        self._map_sequence += 1
725	        record = self._map_change_record(self._map_sequence, actual_added, actual_removed)
726	        self.map_changes.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
727	        self.replay.append(copy.deepcopy(record))
728	        self._reroute_after_map_change()
729	        self._reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change()
730	        return copy.deepcopy(record)

732	    def _map_change_record(
733	        self, sequence: int, added: list[Position], removed: list[Position]
734	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
735	        return {
736	            "type": "map_change",
737	            "tick": self.tick,
738	            "sequence": sequence,
739	            "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
740	            "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
741	        }

743	    def _plan_route(
744	        self, robot: Robot, task: Task, start: Position | None = None
745	    ) -> list[Position] | None:
746	        """Shortest current->pickup->dropoff route, or None if unreachable.
747	
748	        *start* overrides the robot's current position, which is how sidestep
749	        candidates are evaluated without moving the robot first. The
750	        pickup/delivery rule itself is shared with first-time assignment and
751	        checkpoint validation via :func:`_plan_task_route`.
752	        """
753	        origin = robot.position if start is None else start
754	        return _plan_task_route(self.grid, origin, task)

756	    def _reroute_after_map_change(self) -> None:
757	        for task in self.tasks.values():
758	            if task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
759	                continue
760	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
761	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
762	                continue
763	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
764	            if route is None:
765	                robot.route = []
766	                self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
767	            else:
768	                # Only the route is refreshed here; pickup/delivery are
769	                # confirmed at step start (or were already recorded).
770	                robot.route = route
771	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)

773	    def _recover_paused_tasks(self) -> None:
774	        """Resume tasks suspended by map unreachability where possible."""
775	        for task_id in sorted(self.paused_tasks):
776	            task = self.tasks.get(task_id)
777	            if task is None or task.completed or task.assigned_robot is None:
778	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
779	                continue
780	            robot = self.robots[task.assigned_robot]
781	            if robot.task_id != task.task_id:
782	                self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
783	                continue
784	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
785	            if route is None:
786	                robot.route = []
787	                continue
788	            robot.route = route
789	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task_id)
790	            self._finish_if_arrived(robot)

796	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
797	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
798	        cells: set[Position] = set()
799	        for robot in self.robots.values():
800	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
801	                cells.update(robot.route)
802	        return cells

804	    def _safe_side_cells(
805	        self,
806	        robot: Robot,
807	        occupied: Mapping[Position, str],
808	        reserved: Mapping[Position, str],
809	        forbidden: Iterable[Position] = (),
810	    ) -> Iterator[Position]:
811	        """Adjacent cells *robot* may actually side-step onto this tick.
812	
813	        The very same safety rule backs every side-step decision -- an idle
814	        robot yielding for someone, a busy robot dodging a blocker itself, and
815	        the hypothetical leave checks behind a retreat -- so the shared
816	        conditions live exactly here. A cell qualifies only when it:
817	
818	        * lies inside the map with no obstacle (``GridMap.neighbors`` already
819	          skips anything else),
820	        * is held by no robot in the given (possibly hypothetical) layout,
821	        * was not reserved by a move that already happened this tick,
822	        * lies on no other robot's remaining route (the moving robot's own
823	          route is excluded), and
824	        * is not among *forbidden*: cells that are physically free but unsafe
825	          for the caller's scenario, such as the requester's own cell (a
826	          side-step there would swap the two robots within one tick) or the
827	          retreating requester's replanned path (parking there only moves the
828	          blockage onto a cell the requester must re-enter).
829	
830	        Neighbours are yielded in the deterministic ``GridMap.neighbors``
831	        order (up, left, right, down); callers keep their own selection rules.
832	        """
833	        blocked = set(forbidden)
834	        blocked.update(self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id))
835	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(robot.position):
836	            if cell in blocked or cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
837	                continue
838	            yield cell

840	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
841	        self,
842	        blocker: Robot,
843	        requester: Robot,
844	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
845	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
846	    ) -> Position | None:
847	        """Free side-cell a parked blocker can yield to, or None.
848	
849	        Only a robot with no bound task and no remaining route is parked and
850	        asked to yield; callers must never route a taskless-but-moving robot
851	        here. The requester's own cell is forbidden (yielding onto it would
852	        swap the two robots within one tick); every other safety condition is
853	        shared via :meth:`_safe_side_cells`, so the blocker never trades one
854	        blockage for another. The first candidate in neighbour order wins.
855	        """
856	        return next(
857	            self._safe_side_cells(
858	                blocker, occupied, reserved, forbidden=(requester.position,)
859	            ),
860	            None,
861	        )

863	    def _self_sidestep(
864	        self,
865	        robot: Robot,
866	        task: Task | None,
867	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
868	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
869	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
870	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
871	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
872	
873	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
874	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
875	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
876	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
877	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
878	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
879	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
880	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
881	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
882	        """
883	        if task is None or task.completed:
884	            return None
885	        destination = robot.route[0]
886	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
887	        if blocker_id is None:
888	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
889	        best: tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None = None
890	        best_length = 0
891	        # Candidates arrive in neighbour order (up, left, right, down), so the
892	        # first candidate of the minimum replanned length automatically keeps
893	        # that order as the tie break.
894	        for cell in self._safe_side_cells(robot, occupied, reserved):
895	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
896	            if route is None:
897	                continue
898	            if (
899	                blocker_id is not None
900	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
901	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(

914	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
915	        self,
916	        robot: Robot,
917	        side: Position,
918	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
919	        blocker_id: str,
920	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
921	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
922	        already_moved: frozenset[str],

924	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
925	
926	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
927	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
928	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
929	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
930	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
931	        never rejected here.
932	        """
933	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
934	            return False
935	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
936	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
937	            return False
938	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
939	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
940	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
941	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
942	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id

944	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
945	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
946	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
947	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
948	        return not self._can_vacate(
949	            blocker,
950	            robot,
951	            hyp_occupied,
952	            reserved,
953	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
954	            blocked_path,
955	        )

957	    def _can_vacate(
958	        self,
959	        blocker: Robot,
960	        requester: Robot,
961	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
962	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
963	        checking: frozenset[str],
964	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
965	    ) -> bool:
966	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
967	
968	        A parked blocker (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
969	        yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; a moving
970	        blocker -- task-bound, or taskless but still driving a remaining route
971	        -- leaves by driving onto its next waypoint (possibly following a
972	        chain of robots that all move this tick); a task-bound one may also
973	        sidestep onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by map
974	        unreachability never move. *checking* names robots already on the
975	        dependency chain (including robots that used their one move of this
976	        tick), so meeting one again closes a cyclic dependency -- a head-on
977	        deadlock, or the requester itself -- and never proves an exit merely
978	        because every robot on the cycle still carries a route.
979	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive
980	        back through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so
981	        such sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on
982	        the blocker's own route does).
983	
984	        The follow chain can run through an arbitrarily long legal queue, so
985	        the search is an explicit stack rather than Python recursion: a queue
986	        of twelve hundred robots ending at a parked robot with no side cell
987	        must report "cannot vacate" from a normal ``step()`` instead of
988	        raising :class:`RecursionError`. Each frame is
989	        ``(robot, checking, resume)``. A frame examined for the first time
990	        first tries the free-waypoint and follow-chain rules; only when the
991	        chain ahead comes back empty does it resume at its own side-cell
992	        scan, which is exactly the order the single recursive call imposed.
993	        """
994	        stack: list[tuple[Robot, frozenset[str], bool]] = [(blocker, checking, False)]
995	        while stack:
996	            current, current_checking, resume = stack.pop()
997	            if current.robot_id in current_checking:
998	                # The chain has folded back onto a robot it already depends
999	                # on: a cycle cannot vacate itself. The frame that followed
1000	                # this one simply resumes with its own side-cell options.
1001	                continue
1002	            task = self.tasks[current.task_id] if current.task_id is not None else None
1003	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1004	                continue
1005	            if not current.route:
1006	                if task is not None:
1007	                    # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this
1008	                    # tick; it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
1009	                    continue
1010	                # A parked robot (no task and no remaining route) leaves only by
1011	                # yielding onto a safe side cell for the requesting robot; it does
1012	                # so onto the first safe cell in neighbour order. When that
1013	                # particular cell sits on the path the retreating requester must
1014	                # re-enter, parking there only relocates the blockage instead of
1015	                # clearing it, so it does not count as leaving.
1016	                side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(current, requester, occupied, reserved)
1017	                if side is not None and side not in blocked_path:
1018	                    return True
1019	                continue
1020	            if not resume:
1021	                ahead = current.route[0]
1022	                if (
1023	                    self.grid.traversable(ahead)
1024	                    and ahead not in occupied
1025	                    and ahead not in reserved
1026	                ):
1027	                    return True
1028	                occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
1029	                if (
1030	                    occupant_id is not None
1031	                    and occupant_id != current.robot_id
1032	                    and occupant_id not in current_checking
1033	                ):
1034	                    # The robot could follow the occupant once that robot
1035	                    # vacates its cell this same tick. This frame resumes with
1036	                    # its side-cell scan only after the chain ahead proves it
1037	                    # cannot clear, mirroring the recursive call order.
1038	                    stack.append((current, current_checking, True))
1039	                    stack.append(
1040	                        (
1041	                            self.robots[occupant_id],
1042	                            current_checking | {current.robot_id},
1043	                            False,
1044	                        )
1045	                    )
1046	                    continue
1047	            if task is None:
1048	                # A taskless robot that still drives a remaining route never
1049	                # sidesteps off it -- not even to unblock a requester -- so a side
1050	                # cell cannot count as a way out for it.
1051	                continue
1052	            # Otherwise the task-bound blocker might sidestep onto a free side
1053	            # cell itself, but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has
1054	            # to use -- parking there only moves the blockage.
1055	            for side_cell in self._safe_side_cells(
1056	                current, occupied, reserved, forbidden=blocked_path
1057	            ):
1058	                if self._plan_route(current, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
1059	                    return True
1060	        return False

1062	    def _update_traffic_waits(
1063	        self,
1064	        waited: dict[str, str],
1065	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
1066	    ) -> None:
1067	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
1068	
1069	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
1070	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
1071	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
1072	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
1073	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
1074	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
1075	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
1076	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
1077	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
1078	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
1079	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
1080	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
1081	        """
1082	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1083	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
1084	        for robot_id in waited:
1085	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
1086	                continue
1087	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
1088	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
1089	                continue
1090	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
1091	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1092	                continue
1093	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
1094	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
1095	                continue
1096	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
1097	            if entry is None:
1098	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
1099	            else:
1100	                surviving[robot_id] = {
1101	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
1102	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
1103	                }
1104	        self._traffic_waits = surviving

1106	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
1107	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
1108	
1109	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
1110	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
1111	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
1112	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
1113	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
1114	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
1115	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
1116	        """
1117	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
1118	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
1119	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
1120	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
1121	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
1122	                continue
1123	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
1124	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]

1128	            {

1140	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
1141	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest available robot using stable tie breaks.
1142	
1143	        Only a robot with no bound task *and* no remaining route is available:
1144	        a taskless robot still driving a preset route keeps that route and is
1145	        never selected, even when it is the closest to the pickup -- being
1146	        temporarily blocked by traffic does not count as having finished the
1147	        route either. Skipping such a robot never touches its position,
1148	        mileage, cargo state or remaining waypoints, and never makes other
1149	        tasks wait: the next available robot is chosen by the usual shortest
1150	        feasible route length with the robot id string as tie break.
1151	        """
1152	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
1153	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
1154	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
1155	            for robot in self.robots.values():
1156	                if not robot.idle or robot.route:
1157	                    continue
1158	                route = _plan_task_route(self.grid, robot.position, task)
1159	                if route is None:
1160	                    continue
1161	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
1162	            if not choices:
1163	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
1164	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
1165	                continue
1166	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
1167	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
1168	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
1169	            robot.route = route
1170	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id

1177	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
1178	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
1179	                task.picked_up = True

1189	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
1190	        moved: list[str] = []

1194	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
1195	            del occupied[robot.position]
1196	            robot.position = destination
1197	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
1198	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
1199	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
1200	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
1201	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
1202	
1203	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
1204	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:

1206	                continue
1207	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
1208	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
1209	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
1210	                continue
1211	            if not robot.route:

1213	                continue
1214	            destination = robot.route[0]
1215	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
1216	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
1217	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
1218	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
1219	                    if route is None:

1221	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
1222	                    else:
1223	                        robot.route = route

1229	                relocate(robot, destination)
1230	                robot.route.pop(0)
1231	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
1232	                continue
1233	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
1234	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
1235	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]

1251	                if blocker.route:

1254	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)

1279	            "moved": moved,

1358	            },
